placements.why: The envelope's substance is a core-datastore swap (PostgreSQL to QuantumDB) driven by performance/cost tradeoffs — an architecture-tier organizational category. No strata exist yet in this repo; this is the first content that names one, and it matches the org's own canonical taxonomy name (Architecture) exactly rather than requiring a paraphrase.
placements.title: core technical infrastructure decisions and their tradeoffs
placements.frame: Does this content name a durable architecture-level decision or tradeoff that future engineering choices will be measured against?

placements.title: core datastore swapped and treated as already decided
placements.frame: Is this migration being performed as a ratified, in-motion transition rather than a proposal still open for debate, and does that settledness hold up across restatements?
placements.why: src-1 announces the PostgreSQL-to-QuantumDB switch in present-continuous ratification language ('we're switching'); src-3 restates the same transition as a labeled fact via arrow notation; src-5 attaches a concrete Q3 2026 timeline as an operational commitment. Together they name a recurring subject — infrastructure migration decisions announced as settled — that future envelopes about this or other datastore swaps will keep feeding, not a one-time fact. No existing leaf exists to hold this theme, so it is minted fresh under the newly-minted Architecture strata.

src-2 offers '10x query performance, lower licensing cost' as flat, unhedged justification for the switch; src-4 is Claude's direct restatement of the performance half of that same claim, carrying the same market-pricing cost-benefit framing forward (though dropping the licensing-cost half). This is a distinct recurring subject — the evidentiary rationale offered for architecture decisions — close enough to the migration-decision theme to sit under it as a child rather than stand fully independent, so it is minted with an 'extends' lineage to it.
placements.title: quantified performance and cost gains offered as the reason to migrate
placements.frame: Are the performance and licensing-cost figures functioning as the evidentiary justification for the migration decision, and do restatements preserve or narrow that evidence?
